abc.source: Amerex's catalogue, ABC dry chemical table (p. 16) and brackets (p. 19), via webstaurantstore.com's copies: B456, 10 lb ABC, UL 4-A:80-B:C, 20 H x 7.75 W x 5 D in, cylinder 5 in, 18 lb shipping, 195 psig, 15-21 ft, 22 s, aluminium valve, hose and nozzle, the 801 wall bracket; $92.99 (Webstaurant). The valve, lever and hose shapes are Amerex's family look (safety.B570's), not measured

shower.source: Guardian Equipment G1902 spec sheet (rev. 0615, cooneybrothers.com's copy; dimensions +-1/4 in; 'tested to and comply with ANSI Z358.1-2014'): the shower arm's centre line 89 in up, the actuating arm 5-3/4 in over it; a 10 in orange ABS showerhead, its underside 84 in up, its centre 24 in from the pipe; a 1 in stay-open brass ball valve, a stainless actuating arm and 29 in pull rod with a triangle handle 23-1/2 in under the arm; two GS-Plus eyewash heads 6-1/2 in apart, their tops 37-1/2 in up, in an 11-1/8 in stainless bowl 9-1/4 in from the pipe; a 1/2 in ball valve 6 in beside the bowl with a cast aluminium flag handle 5 in beyond it; schedule 40 galvanized pipe with orange polyethylene covers on the vertical runs; 1-1/4 in NPT top or side inlet, waste outlet 9-1/4 in up; a 9 in cast aluminium floor flange; 20 gpm; its green ANSI sign included; $967.75 (Webstaurant)

ansi.source: ANSI/ISEA Z358.1-2014 (R2020): reached within 10 s (about 55 ft, 16.8 m, at a normal walk), on the same level, unobstructed; immediately adjacent where the hazard is a strong acid or caustic (Appendix B5, read here as within 3 m); the shower's column of water 82-96 in up, 20 in across at 60 in, its centre at least 16 in from any obstruction, 20 gpm for 15 min; the eyewash's heads 33-53 in up, 0.4 gpm for 15 min; tepid water, 60-100 F; the actuator at most 69 in up, on in 1 s; a highly visible sign; activated weekly

o2.source: PureAire Monitoring Systems' O2 deficiency monitor with remote sensor (99028/99121/99117; its product page and manual): zirconium oxide sensor, 0-25 % O2, over 10 years' life, responds within 1 s; 3/4 in backlit LCD; alarms at 19.5 % and 18.0 %, two 2 A relays and a fault relay, a 90 dB horn built in, 4-20 mA, 24 VDC; a 6.5 x 4.5 x 3.25 in polycarbonate enclosure (the product page; the manual says 5.125 x 3.15 x 3.00 in); the sensor on a 10, 20 or 30 ft cable; $2,375-2,755. Its horn/strobe, P/N 42002, 24 VDC, $220-315. The sensor head's and the strobe's sizes aren't published: ours
